subject: Polymer: Post-deploy degradation — priority incident and exec sync
messages:
From: Elaine Duong <elaine@polymer.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@polymer.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors after v2-quantize rollout — urgent

Hi Vanessa / Marissa,

We pushed the v2-quantized model (model-id: rwd-model-v2-q3) to production at ~07:20 PT. Within ~10 minutes we started seeing a spike in 429s and backend 5xx errors from your API (samples attached). Clients are also reporting timeouts and heavy retry traffic.

Impact: several customer integrations experienced request failures and significant tail latency. Our SREs see a correlated increase in queued requests and per-instance CPU/kernel stalls. We rolled back client-side to v1 to get immediate relief but the platform shows persistent elevated error rates for a subset of routes.

Attachments: polymer_error_samples.log (excerpted), timeline.csv (internal)

Can you confirm if this rollout included any kernel selection or KV cache changes? We need an ETA on a mitigation — this is impacting billing and customer SLAs.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Duong
Sr. Engineer, Production Systems
Polymer.ai

Forwarding incoming from Polymer (thread below). Priority incident — escalating to infra and ops.

Immediate asks:
- Rishi: please triage kernel/quantization path and confirm if the rollout changed kernel selection heuristics or KV cache policies. Share quick mitigation steps (rollback vs config flips).
- Hannah: please loop in incident comms and exec ops; Marissa will manage account communications and credits.
- Marissa: set up a 30-min exec sync with Polymer for 12:00 PT (19:00 UTC) and offer temporary traffic shaping.

I attached the rollback runbook (runbook_rollbacks_v3.pdf). If rollback is required we should target a stage rollback ASAP and isolate affected model variant.

Vanessa Ortiz

Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 08:39:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors after v2-quantize rollout — urgent

On Tue, Jul 20, 2026 at 08:28 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding incoming from Polymer (thread below). Priority incident — escalating to infra and ops.

Initial triage (first 15m):
- Observed behavior: specific to model variant rwd-model-v2-q3 on A100-p4d nodes with kernel-set K23. Error modes: 429s (request queue overflow) and 502/504 from the inference service when the KV-cache eviction thrashing occurs.
- Trigger: a kernel selector tweak in the deploy manifest enabled an aggressive prefetch/batching optimization intended to improve throughput. That optimization appears to increase KV-cache churn at short seq lengths and reduces effective cache hits under the current request distribution. Result: increased per-request latency, queue build-up, and backpressure -> 429 at the router.

Short-term mitigations to apply in this order (can do within 10-20m):
1) Disable aggressive batching/prefetch flag in routing rules for rwd-model-v2-q3.
2) Temporarily pause model variant on a subset of nodes (canary rollback to v1 on p4d A100 pool).
3) Increase per-worker request timeout and bump max inflight requests per worker to reduce router 429s (tradeoff: potential higher tail latency).
4) Apply per-customer token-based throttle for Polymer to limit retries (rate-limit keys at edge).

I will push a hotfix to kernel selector config and prepare a stage rollback. Logs and top stack traces are attached (deploy-manifest-v2.json referenced).

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 09:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors after v2-quantize rollout — urgent

Elaine — really sorry for the impact here. We take incidents like this seriously.

We've initiated mitigations: Rishi is rolling a config flip and preparing a rollback; Vanessa's team is coordinating the timeline. We propose the following immediate steps from Redwood's side:
- Apply temporary rate limit on Polymer account keys to dampen retry amplification.
- Begin a staged rollback of the v2-quantized variant on the A100 pool (target completion 09:00 PT).
- Provide a one-time service credit for measured customer downtime — I'll follow up with Finance and include a proposed credit range within 24h.

Can you confirm whether your SREs can hold off client retries for the next 30 minutes while we flip configs and complete rollback? Also request any sample request IDs that still show 504 to correlate logs.

I'll schedule the exec sync for 12:00 PT and send calendar invite. Thanks for flagging this quickly.

—Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts

Thanks — we paused client retries and opened an internal incident. We confirm the rollback to v1 on the problematic A100 pool reduced 429/5xx rates within ~18 minutes of the flip; tail latency is improving.

Request prior to the exec sync: can Redwood temporarily apply a per-key throttle to keep inbound TPS for Polymer under 50 req/s until we complete a coordinated rollout and postmortem? That will prevent the retry amplification we observed.

We'll join the 12:00 PT call and share additional logs. Appreciate the rapid response.

Elaine
